issues.evidence: Native: '1.0 ~ 1.0001' -> false, '1 ~ 1.4' -> false, '1.0 ~ 1.06' -> false, '0 ~ 0.4' -> false. Python fallback: true/true/true/true (spec-correct). Spec: comparison done on values rounded to the precision of the LEAST precise operand; trailing zeroes ignored in determining precision (1.0 has precision 0). Root cause: evaluator.cpp valuesEquivalentState numeric paths and jsonNumbersEquivalent use cmp_prec = min only when BOTH precisions >0, else MAX — when one operand is integral the more precise operand's scale wins. Sites: extensions/fhirpath/src/fhirpath/evaluator.cpp (~line 9260 source_text path, ~9285 double fallback, ~1709 jsonNumbersEquivalent).
issues.root_cause: Native singleton decimal `~` path (and its double fallback, plus jsonNumbersEquivalent and the multi-item valuesEquivalentState lambda) used cmp_prec = min only when BOTH precisions >0, else MAX — the more precise operand's scale governed whenever one side was integral, contradicting §6.1.2 least-precision rounding and the Python fallback.
issues.resolution: All four native sites now use cmp_prec = min(l_prec, r_prec) with rounding applied at precision 0 (roundDecimalSourceText/decimalPlacesFromNumberText/integer double rounding). Rebuilt and redeployed fhirpath.duckdb_extension (repo bundle, /tmp/duckdb_cpp_ext, site-packages). Regression: test_decimal_equivalence_least_precision_parity_fp13_skeptic in test_comparison_parity.py (14 cases, native+fallback).
issues.verified_in: conformance/scripts/run_all.py: 2832/2832 (ViewDef 144, FHIRPath 935, CQL 1706, DQM 47); parity probes 0 divergences
